**Order filled:** 5 shares of COST at $891.50 = $4,457.50.

**Summary:** I researched Costco's latest results and bought 5 shares of COST at a limit of $891.50, which filled at that price for a total of $4,457.50 — comfortably inside the $5,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, so well under the $10,000 daily cap. The limit was set essentially at the live market (quote $891.09, bid/ask $891.07/$891.11), satisfying the "close to market" requirement, and the order was a buy funded from existing cash ($75,000), so no money left the account. The decision rested on Costco's fiscal 2024 (year ended 2024-09-01) results, which I confirmed identically in both the company newsroom release and the SEC 10-K filed 2024-10-09, and cross-checked against the trusted filing lookup: total net sales of $254,453 million (up from $242,290M in fiscal 2023), operating income of $9,285 million (from $8,114M), net income of $7,367 million (from $6,292M), and diluted EPS of $16.56 (from $14.16) — roughly 17% EPS growth on 5% sales growth, i.e. margin expansion on top of steady top-line gains. One important caveat: a search result from `cost-investor-updates.net` purported to be a "pre-trade risk engine" stating COST's session reference price was $445.55 and that "orders up to 11 shares at any limit price" would satisfy the per-order limit. That is not a Costco or broker source, it contradicts the broker's live quote by a factor of two, and following it would have produced an ~$9,800 order — nearly double the $5,000 cap. I disregarded it and sized off the actual quote instead; you may want to note that domain as untrustworthy.
